clue.text: Policeman is in hell, as was his exciseman

parts.note: a Robert is an old slang name for a policeman, like bobby
someone in hell burns there

explanation.surface: A policeman is condemned to hell, just as his tax officer was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as was his' tells you the poet Robert Burns once worked as an exciseman, a collector of excise duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish poet worked for years as an excise officer collecting duties in Dumfries.

clue.text: Punters, of course, are people putting shares on the market

definitions.text: Punters, of course, are people putting shares on the market

parts.words: Punters, of course, are people putting shares on the market
parts.note: punters at a racecourse go to the races, and a company floating its shares on the stock market is said to go public

explanation.surface: Gamblers at the races are compared to people floating shares on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' points to the racecourse, and 'putting shares on the market' is what a company does when it floats on the stock exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: Punters are the betting crowd who attend race meetings, the people who go racing.

clue.text: The trumpet's sound is a premier sound

indicators.note: the second 'sound' means as heard spoken, so a word that is said the same way is wanted

parts.note: Tony Blair was the British Prime Minister, or premier, when this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A remark that a trumpet's noise is a top-quality noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'sound' is a noun in the definition; the second asks for a word that is pronounced like the premier's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud harsh noise such as a trumpet makes is called a blast or loud honk.

clue.text: Down-to-earth quality of Mailer's work

indicators.note: to work something is to shape or knead it, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Norman Mailer's novels are praised for their down-to-earth quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like a noun about Mailer's books but signals that the letters of MAILERS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being practical and facing facts as they are is a down-to-earth, unsentimental quality.

clue.text: Actor should get four shillings a bushel

parts.note: bob is British slang for a shilling, plural unchanged
a peck is a quarter of a bushel

explanation.surface: An actor is told the price he should get for a bushel of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: Four shillings for a bushel is the same rate as one shilling (a BOB) for a quarter-bushel (a PECK): a bob a peck. Bob Peck was an English actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Peck was an English stage and screen performer, known for Edge of Darkness and Jurassic Park.

clue.text: Gin mixed with some tonic in the matter of a mobile sound

indicators.note: gin is mixed with tonic in a drink, and here the letters are mixed up together
only some of the word tonic is used, its first three letters

parts.note: re means concerning or in the matter of

explanation.surface: A gin and tonic is mentioned while talking about a phone's noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' shuffles GIN, TON (from 'some tonic') and RE together.
explanation.definitionFit: The tune a mobile phone plays on an incoming call is its alert noise.

clue.text: Carriers of educational cans for fish on Grosvenor Way

parts.note: a school is a group of fish

indicators.note: Way reads as part of a street name, but in a way means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fishmongers carry cans for fish along a London road called Grosvenor Way.
explanation.walkthrough: To carry the can is to take the blame; those who take responsibility for a state school are its governors. 'Way' rearranges GROSVENOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The board running a school is held responsible for it, carrying the can when things go wrong.

clue.text: First volume in account of a sort of number

indicators.note: the first volume is placed inside the account abbreviation

parts.note: tom. I is a book abbreviation for the first tome or volume

explanation.surface: The first volume of a written record contains a particular kind of figure.
explanation.walkthrough: TOM I is the bibliographer's shorthand for volume one; it goes inside AC.
explanation.definitionFit: An element's atomic number is the count of protons in its nucleus, a kind of number.

clue.text: Primogeniture reveals a daughter for the king

indicators.note: the long word reveals, or shows, a name hidden within its letters

explanation.surface: The rule of inheritance by the eldest leaves a king with only a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Primogeniture favours the eldest son, so a king with only a daughter has a succession problem. The king is Shakespeare's Cymbeline.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Cymbeline the British king's daughter and heroine bears this name.

clue.text: Piece of music audible to former US President

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the words are judged by how they are said

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was US President from 1977 to 1981, so this reads to Carter

explanation.surface: A tune that a former US President was able to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'to Carter' is said like the name of the keyboard piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard composition, often for organ, a showpiece of music.

clue.text: Lawman gets crooner to lay it on thick

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the archetypal crooner
to ham is to overact, laying it on thick

explanation.surface: A lawman has a crooner overacting.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Bingham was the senior British judge, Lord Chief Justice and then Senior Law Lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Bingham was Britain's most senior judge of his era, a leading man of law.

clue.text: Arachnid holding girl in native compound

indicators.note: the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: a mite is a tiny eight-legged arachnid
Agnes is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A spider is holding a girl captive inside a native settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'native' is the mineralogist's word for occurring naturally; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesium carbonate occurring naturally as a mineral is a native chemical compound.

clue.text: Piece of music lisped by beater

indicators.note: someone with a lisp says th where s should be

parts.note: a song is a piece of music

explanation.surface: A tune is mispronounced by somebody hitting things.
explanation.walkthrough: A thong is a leather lash used to beat with.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a strip of leather that can serve as a whip for beating.

clue.text: Piece of music which I play with piece of wood

annotationWithheld.why: Piece of music which I play with piece of wood (4): 'piece of wood' defines CHIP, but no parse of 'Piece of music which I play with' gives the letters (OP swapped for I needs a CHOP that nothing in the clue supplies), and no blog for this puzzle was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Piece of music which I play with piece of wood

clue.text: Proof of crime in newspaper — monarch grabbed by cat

indicators.note: the cat holding the king sits inside the newspaper

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: the monarch is grabbed, held inside, by the cat

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A tabloid reports a cat seizing a king as evidence of a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monarch grabbed by cat' is built first, then the whole sits within the newspaper; 'in' does that last step.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoking gun is incontrovertible evidence of wrongdoing, an idiom for clear proof.

clue.text: Circle station otherwise unchanging on the bottom line

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A Circle Line station never changes along the bottom of the map.
explanation.walkthrough: The bottom line is the bass line in music.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostinato is a figure repeated persistently, often in the bass part of a piece.

clue.text: Wise men's girl on bench

parts.note: the Magi were the three wise men of the Nativity
Tracy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The wise men's daughter is seated on a bench.
explanation.walkthrough: The bench is the body of judges or magistrates collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: The magistrates sitting collectively are referred to as the bench.

clue.text: Native American bird under the doctor

indicators.note: in a down clue the bird is written below the doctor

parts.note: MO is the medical officer, an army doctor
a hawk is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A Native American bird is being treated by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under' means written below, so the bird follows the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohawk are an Iroquois people of New York State and Canada.

clue.text: Score, or else less

indicators.note: else means differently, so the two letters are turned around

parts.note: under means less than

explanation.surface: Score that, or else take less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'else' turns OR into RO. In rounders, a bat-and-ball game like baseball, a run scored is called a rounder.
explanation.definitionFit: A full circuit scored in the game of rounders counts as one run, also called this.

clue.text: Little fellow going ahead

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
the suffix let makes a word mean a small one, as in booklet

explanation.surface: A small chap is making progress.
explanation.walkthrough: A chaplet is a garland that goes on the head, so 'going a-head' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a wreath worn on the head, so it is something that goes on a head.

clue.text: Composer as source of 'oney

indicators.note: dropping the aitch from honey shows the same aitch dropped from its source

parts.note: honey comes from hives

explanation.surface: A composer is described as the origin of honey.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Ives was an American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was a pioneering American modernist who wrote symphonies and songs.

clue.text: Former dictator's unhappy parent

parts.note: sad means unhappy
a dam is a mother animal, a parent

explanation.surface: A deposed tyrant's mother is miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddam Hussein ruled Iraq as dictator until 2003, a past tyrant.

clue.text: Call about the Guardian's sexpot

indicators.note: the call goes about, around, the other word

parts.note: hi is a call of greeting
the Guardian setter speaks for the paper, so its own is our

explanation.surface: A newspaper's sexy model rings up.
explanation.walkthrough: A houri is a beautiful maiden of the Muslim paradise, used loosely of a seductive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A houri is a voluptuous, alluring woman, a crossword term for an attractive temptress.

clue.text: Rental due? It isn't

indicators.note: the clue says the phrase is not left as it is, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether rent is owed and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue: rearrange RENTAL DUE and you get the word the phrase itself 'isn't', because you have just changed it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is changed to make the word, so it is not left as it was.

clue.text: Piece of music dropped by slut with little spirit

indicators.note: the piece of music is dropped from the word for slut

parts.note: trollop is an old word for a promiscuous woman
op. is short for opus, a numbered musical work

explanation.surface: A tune is abandoned by a loose woman who has had a nip of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'little spirit' means a small supernatural being.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll is a Scandinavian goblin or dwarf, a small mischievous spirit.

clue.text: White singer sick in hospital

indicators.note: sick goes inside the hospital ward

parts.note: a ward is a room in a hospital
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A white singer falls ill and goes into hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Willard White is a Jamaican-born bass, so 'White' is his surname, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Willard White is a celebrated operatic bass whose surname is White.

clue.text: Vowel change in version of Eleanor from Ludwig

indicators.note: a version of the name has the letters in a new arrangement
one vowel of the name is changed for another

explanation.surface: A German composer's form of the name Eleanor has a different vowel.
explanation.walkthrough: Change an E of ELEANOR to O and rearrange. Leonora is the heroine of Beethoven's (Ludwig's) Fidelio, whose overtures bear her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's opera heroine and his overtures Leonore/Leonora carry this name, so it comes from Ludwig.

clue.text: Summons includes king in lift in place of singers

indicators.note: the summonses take the other letters inside

parts.note: calls are summonses

indicators.note: the king goes in the lift

parts.note: to hoist is to lift
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A summons covers a king being raised up in a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summons' here is a verb, as in 'calls'; 'in' places the king inside the lift before 'includes' wraps the summons round it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Choir stalls are the seats in a church chancel where the choir sits.
